title: The Quran: Surah 94, ash-Sharh (The Soothing)
author: Tradução inglesa de Talal Itani (ClearQuran)
tradition: Texto sagrado do Islão, século VII
intro: Lição sobre a Surata 94. O texto inglês é a tradução de Talal Itani, reproduzida sem alterações; as notas de língua, perguntas, discussão e escrita são material pedagógico separado, baseado apenas no que o próprio texto diz.

source.title: Quran English Translation: Clear, Pure, Easy to Read Modern English
source.edition: Edition A (uses the word 'Allah' to refer to the Creator)

questions.q: What comes with hardship, according to verse 5?
questions.why: O versículo 5 diz: 'With hardship comes ease.'
O versículo 3 diz que o fardo 'weighed down your back'.

questions.q: Verses 5 and 6 repeat the same sentence. What does the repetition suggest?
options: That the sentence is a mistake
That the idea is important and should be remembered
That the text is about to end
questions.why: A repetição exacta dá ênfase à ideia.

questions.q: What kind of sentences are verses 7 and 8?
questions.why: 'Turn to devotion' e 'turn for everything' são ordens.

questions.q: Which sentence best sums up the passage?
options: It tells a story about a journey
It reminds the speaker of what was done for him, says hardship comes with ease, and ends with instructions
questions.why: Os versículos 1 a 4 recordam, os versículos 5 e 6 afirmam e os versículos 7 e 8 instruem.

B2.discussion: 'With hardship comes ease.' Can you think of a situation where this idea is true? Explain.
B2.writing: Write 80 to 100 words: Say what the verses tell the reader to do and why.

questions.q: What does verse 7 tell the reader to do when his work is done?
questions.why: O versículo 7 diz: 'When your work is done, turn to devotion.'

questions.q: 'Raised for you your reputation' (verse 4) means his reputation was:
Verses 1 to 4 look back at what has already been done. How might they prepare verses 5 and 6?
options: By giving past examples that support the statement about hardship and ease
questions.why: Os versículos 1 a 4 recordam o que já foi feito, e os versículos 5 e 6 afirmam a regra.

options: Both give instructions using the verb 'turn'
questions.why: 'Turn to devotion' e 'turn for everything' repetem o verbo 'turn'.

options: The passage moves from the past to a general statement and then to instructions
The passage moves from instructions to a story
questions.why: Versículos 1 a 4: o que foi feito. Versículos 5 e 6: afirmação. Versículos 7 e 8: instruções.

C1.discussion: The first four verses look back, verses 5 and 6 state a rule, and verses 7 and 8 look forward. What does this three-part order do for the reader?
C1.writing: Write 120 to 150 words: Explain how the repeated sentence in verses 5 and 6 connects the two halves of the passage.

questions.why: Os versículos 5 e 6 dizem exactamente 'With hardship comes ease.'

options: a physical image for the burden named in verse 2
questions.why: O fardo do versículo 2 é descrito no versículo 3 como algo que pesava nas costas.

questions.q: 'With hardship comes ease' uses 'with', not 'after'. What does this word choice suggest?
options: That ease comes together with hardship, not only afterwards
questions.why: 'With' sugere que o alívio vem junto com a dificuldade.

questions.q: The passage ends with two instructions that use 'turn'. What does the repetition do?
options: It ties the two commands together and closes the passage with a clear direction
questions.why: 'Turn to devotion' e 'turn for everything' repetem o verbo e fecham o texto.

options: Reminders of the past (1 to 4), a repeated statement at the centre (5 and 6), two closing instructions (7 and 8)
questions.why: A frase repetida fica no centro do texto, entre os lembretes e as instruções.

C2.discussion: The sentence in verse 5 is repeated exactly in verse 6, at the centre of the passage. What does this do to the rhythm and the meaning?
C2.writing: Write 150 to 200 words: Analyse how the passage is built around the repeated sentence, referring to specific verses and words.
